Totterdown's colourful houses

Updated 20 November 2026. Every claim links to its source. Where sources disagree, we say so. How we check facts.

Totterdown's hillside terraces, many painted in bright colours, are among Bristol's best-known sights. They can be seen from Temple Meads station and from across the city centre. [1] They are people's homes, so look and take photos from the street.

Quick answer

  • Best-known street: Richmond Street, nicknamed the "rainbow row", with more than 70 houses, most of them brightly painted. [2] [3]
  • Best viewpoints: from below on Clarence Road by the New Cut, which looks up at the Richmond Street terrace, and from the approach to Temple Meads station. [3] [4]
  • Why are they painted? Nobody has documented how it began. The popular stories are local legends, and the sources disagree. [1] [5]
  • Worth knowing: residents campaigned in 2022 to protect the view of the houses from new development near the station. [4] [6]

Which streets in Totterdown have colourful houses?

Totterdown's best-known colourful street is Richmond Street, the "rainbow row" of more than 70 houses, most of them painted; painted terraces also line Sydenham Road and Henry Street. [2] [3]

Streets to look for
StreetWhat to see
Richmond StreetCrests the northern ridge of Totterdown. The best-known row, with more than 70 houses, most of them painted. The houses on the right-hand side have the best views out over the city. [3] [2]
Sydenham RoadGabled terraced houses in pastel shades. [3]
Henry StreetAnother typical Totterdown street of painted terraces; the Shakespeare pub is here. [3] [7]
Windsor TerraceA hillside terrace in Totterdown, listed by an estate agent as having views over the city. [8]
Vale StreetEngland's steepest residential street, lined with terraced houses. [9]

You can link several of these into a self-guided walk.

Where is the best place to see Totterdown's colourful houses?

The best place to see Totterdown's colourful houses is from below, on Clarence Road beside the Avon New Cut, which looks up at the Richmond Street terrace; the hillside is also visible from Temple Meads station. [3] [1]

  • From below, on Clarence Road: a walking guide says Clarence Road, beside the Avon New Cut, gives the best view of the Richmond Street terrace on the hill behind. [3] [10]
  • From Temple Meads: the hillside is visible from the station and its approach, which is why residents care about the view. [4] [1]
  • From Richmond Street itself: a ridge-top street with views across the city centre. [3]
  • For a view of the city rather than the houses: try Perrett's Park and Victoria Park. [11] [12]

Why are Totterdown's houses painted?

Nobody has documented the origin. Local stories include: [1] [5]

  • Sailors' homes: the popular tale is that returning sailors could spot their homes from a distance. Secret Bristol says it doesn't stand up to much scrutiny. [1]
  • Saving a house: one story has a house painted red to stop it being demolished, with the rest of the terrace following. Sources mostly tell this about Cliftonwood rather than Totterdown. [5] [1]
  • Spare paint: for Totterdown, a local story says a painter with spare paint offered to decorate houses cheaply. [2]

When did it start? A long-time Richmond Street resident dates the trend to the 1960s or 70s, when young people moved into the area and started doing the houses up. [2] The Bristol Cable says the houses on the Totterdown escarpment have been painted in bright colours since the 1980s. [4]

Will new buildings block the view of Totterdown's houses?

Residents campaigned in 2022 under a "save our view" banner against tall buildings planned for Temple Island, below the hill. [4] [6] In April 2026 Bristol City Council approved Legal & General's £350m Temple Island scheme, with 520 homes, offices, a hotel and shops. [13] Objectors argued the buildings would block views of Totterdown's coloured houses from the city. [14] We haven't found a source describing how the approved designs affect the view.

Can you take photos of the houses?

You can photograph from the street, but people live in these houses.

  • Stay on the pavement, and don't block doors, steps or driveways.
  • Keep noise down, especially in the evening and at weekends.
  • Ask before including residents in your photos.
  • The streets are very steep, so wear shoes with grip. How to get here.

Where else in Bristol are there colourful houses?

Totterdown isn't the only painted neighbourhood. Time Out names Cliftonwood, on the other side of the city centre, as the most famous and photographed of Bristol's colourful areas. [15]
